channel.title: Times of San Diego - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Times of San Diego (timesofsandiego.com)

item.title: Balboa Park parking fees are almost here. How to avoid a ticket – and save a buck or two
item.description: A Balboa Park space will range from $2.50 to $16 as of Monday, depending on the spot or lot you're in and if you're a city resident.

item.title: Mustang strikes, kills man sitting in Oceanside median
item.description: Oceanside officers were summoned Friday evening to the intersection of Oceanside Boulevard and College Boulevard.

item.title: Waves, trick plays and eggnog chaos: The Holiday Bowl had it all
item.description: From a surfing snowman to the “Eggnog Dump” – with a daring trick play in-between – the Holiday Bowl was entertaining from beginning to end.

item.title: Misconduct derailed prosecution in Navy’s Fat Leonard scandal. Some defendants are seeking answers
item.description: The 'Fat Leonard' case, the Navy's largest corruption scandal, includes findings of prosecutorial misconduct. Two former officers want accountability.

item.title: Rain still sweeping through San Diego County
item.description: A beach hazard warning for minor coastal flooding in low-lying, flood-prone area for high King Tides is in effect through Monday morning.

item.title: California charging new fees on non-removable batteries
item.description: The fee that customers began to pay in the new year is just one piece of the state’s evolving response to an emerging risk.

item.title: Opinion: Rodeos don’t belong in 2026 — not in San Diego, not anywhere
item.description: This will likely be the last year the rodeo comes to Petco Park, and that is not accidental. Corporate sponsors are waking up to animal suffering.

item.title: San Diego Museum of Art is turning 100 in 2026. We take a look back
item.description: San Diego’s oldest and largest art museum boasts 32,000 works. We take a look at its history in the first of a series marking the museum's big 100.

item.title: Protest planned in Oceanside Sunday against U.S. actions in Venezuela
item.description: The Democratic Club of Carlsbad-Oceanside organized the protest, scheduled for 3 p.m. Sunday at the Oceanside Civic Center.

item.title: MarketInk: San Diego media personalities say they’re forever changed by cancer
item.description: Two prominent members of San Diego’s news media admit they are changed people entering 2026 after their journey with cancer last year.
